cells.tense: You are standing where what you carried gets counted and the count comes out even.
cells.act: tend the resource with responsible care
cells.ask: Look at what you are keeping going and give it the care it actually needs. Nothing piled on top, nothing skimped.
cells.core:
You know what was given up for the thing you stand beside, and the ones who benefit can see it too. The effort and the thanks land in the same week, roughly, and nobody has to argue for it. That is the well-working shape of this: what you carried stays yours and the ones it was carried for know it was carried.

Keep it that way by tending the work rather than the record of the work. Somewhere this operation is open at both ends — those who use it have their story, and you have yours, and both are true. Tend what you are actually keeping alive, at the size it truly is, and leave the account incomplete. The care stays steady when what was given up doesn't need to be recited back to you in the exact words you would choose.
cells.sheetLine: The thanks reaches you, and you're still doing the work.
cells.verb: Putting what was given up in front of the people it was given for
cells.place: Where the scales get set right

cells.tense: You are rehearsing what this will be worth before it is finished being what it is.
cells.act: refine one distinction by close attention
cells.ask: Sharpen the line between what someone asked you for and what you offered on top. Write the extra in one line to no one, then stop.
cells.core:
You are running the ceremony before the work is done. What has not happened yet already has a shape you are preparing for, and that preparation has started deciding things before the ones who will be there with you get a say. It looks like care, and what it is doing is settling the value in private so the real ending cannot surprise you.

Step back one notch and sharpen the difference between the help you were asked for and the help you signed up for. They are not enemies, but if the two stay blurred, the extra becomes something you are owed rather than something you offered. Name the gap and set the pen down. That kind of looking is a practice, and it stays clean while it stays quiet. Hold it loose and it does the work; hold it tight and it turns into another thing to prove.

cells.tense: You are at a door that already shut, holding what was given up for it.
cells.act: carry your own share, all of it
cells.ask: Carry the part of this that is yours alone, all of it, without passing any piece along.
cells.core:
The thing you gave for is behind you. Whether it worked, whether they noticed, whether they still do — none of it is still arriving. What remains is the weight you were holding, still carried, in a place where nobody is left to take it from you. The effort was real; the account is closed, and part of you has not moved out of it.

Do not try to hand the backlog to anyone. Put one piece of actual weight down first, on your side, and make that the whole of today's work. Somewhere in your own life something small has gone untended because the older thing is still filling the space. Tend that. The strength to see the smaller thing through is already yours; it just got drafted into carrying something no one is holding anymore.

cells.tense: You are holding the whole thing up quietly and calling it just how things are.
cells.act: look after what grows with a steady hand
cells.ask: Tend something you keep going that no one thanks you for, and keep it to yourself for now.
cells.core:
You are the reason something in your life still works. That is not a story you are telling; it is just true, you would not frame it that way, and the ones who lean on it have no cause to correct you. What you give up for it has stopped looking like a choice and started looking like landscape that came with the place.

Go back to the plainest version of what you do. Choose something you keep going that has no audience and no ledger, and tend it without tracking what it returns. The point is not to be thanked; the point is to feel your own hands in it, at the size it really is. Tending the smaller thing, the one you picked, is how the effort starts belonging to you again rather than to the ground it stands on.

attempts.check: The signature's record says the cycle completes when sacrifice is publicly honored; the cells do not say that a particular person withholds it or that a history of unseen effort is behind the pattern, since none of that is in the record. A reader could reasonably say that what shows is what they see against what is owed to them, and that the record leaning on outside witness is weaker than what the card actually does in this seat. The asks survive a wrong read because each one only asks for a small action on their own side, and none of them depend on another person or on being seen. The sentence that serves the writer more than them is the balanced kernel's line about standing on the value of what was given up, which sounds like a verdict on their worth rather than a description of a functioning.
